I traced it end to end. Here is what I found.

## The short answer

That email is not a Manus *scheduled task* and it is not Brandon typing in Gmail. It is generated by the **app inside one Manus task: "Vacancy Report App"** — task ID `ZyMNjMqrfWqxl0S7FX0tLV` (54,830 credits, created March 17, 2026, still your open working session for this app).

The Daily Collections Report is one of two email jobs baked into that app's backend, in `emailService.ts` as `sendDailyCollectionsEmail()`, which calls `getPaymentsForDate()` and pulls the FLOW snapshot straight from `propertymax.ai`. It renders inline HTML and hands it to a **Gmail SMTP relay**. `brandonrose2@gmail.com` is the *relay mailbox*, not the author — which is why it looks like it came from Brandon.

## The full chain

| Layer | What it is | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Source task | "Vacancy Report App" `ZyMNjMqrfWqxl0S7FX0tLV` | 36 hits for "Daily Collections", 152 for SMTP, 100 for app password, 313 for Gmail in its transcript |
| Code | `emailService.ts` → `sendDailyCollectionsEmail()` + `getPaymentsForDate()` | July 6, 2026 session: "the scheduled `sendDailyCollectionsEmail` function in `emailService.ts`… when it runs on schedule" |
| Data | PropertyMax.ai FLOW / `propertymax.ai/rest/max/getvacantunits` | Matches the email footer: "Refreshed directly from PropertyMax.ai FLOW data immediately before delivery" |
| Delivery | Gmail SMTP with a 16-character Google App Password | Multiple sessions about creating the App Password at `myaccount.google.com/apppasswords` |
| Sender mailbox, then | `brandonrose2@gmail.com` | "the connected Gmail mailbox (`brandonrose2@gmail.com`)" |
| Schedule | Daily, **1:00 PM Pacific** | Email stamped 1:04 PM; Nov 3: "The previous Admin delivery time was 1:00 PM Pacific" |
| Host that ran the Sept 25 send | Manus-hosted deployment `vacancyapp-42vudntx.manus.space` | The button in the email points there; Railway migration did not happen until Oct 19 |
| Recipients, then | Brandon Rose + Marc Menowitz | Your .msg header |

## What changed since, and why it matters

On **October 19** you told that task *"your site isn't working - use this one instead for the reports"* and gave it `aptcorp-vacancy-report.up.railway.app`. The app moved. Then on **November 3** you rebuilt automatic delivery for the *Vacancy* report as one managed background job in the published Manus app: 1:00 PM Pacific, recipients `ethan@apartmentcorp.com` and `mam@22.bz` only, sender switched to `apartmentcorp44@gmail.com`, with a send-ledger blocking duplicates.

The **Collections** job was deliberately left behind: *"retaining Railway only in untouched legacy Collections code."* So today you have two different delivery engines in the same codebase — the Vacancy report on the new managed job, the Collections report still on the legacy in-process timer.

One caveat I verified directly: the dashboard link inside that Sept 25 email (`vacancyapp-42vudntx.manus.space`) is **stale** — it still renders July 24, 2026 data. Every Collections email carrying that button sends recipients to a dashboard that hasn't refreshed in over three months.

## Two things you may want to decide

1. **The Collections report is the last thing still tied to the old Railway/Gmail-relay path** and it still points at a dead dashboard. I can migrate it onto the same managed job as the Vacancy report and repoint the button at the live app.
2. **The sender identity is a relay, not a person.** If a recipient replies to that email, it goes to `brandonrose2@gmail.com` — worth confirming that's intentional, or moving it to a proper reporting address like `reports@apartmentcorp.com`.

Want me to do either of those, or first produce a one-page map of every outbound email your Manus account can generate so you have the full inventory?

Done — the migration is live. Here's the verified state.

## What changed

The Collections report no longer rides the legacy in-process timer. It now runs on the **same single managed job** as the Vacancy report, sending as its **own separate email** at the same 1:00 PM Pacific slot.

| Item | Verified result |
|---|---|
| Job | `VZyvdDPMbzyNdrdFimtdHj` (single job, both reports) |
| Schedule | Daily, 1:00 PM Pacific, DST-aware — next run **Nov 5, 1:00 PM PT** |
| Sender | **apartmentcorp44@gmail.com** (SMTP envelope sender matched, not just the From header) |
| Recipients | ethan@apartmentcorp.com + mam@22.bz, no CC/BCC |
| Dashboard link | **https://vacancyreport.manus.space** |
| Duplicate protection | Separate saved send record per report, per day |
| Legacy local senders | Disabled |

The September 25 numbers were used as the acceptance test: rendered through the existing Collections template, the fresh FLOW pull produced exactly **$5,572,493.60 expected / $5,331,592.68 collected** across 41 buildings — so the data path and calculations survived the migration. Two test emails (Vacancy and Collections) went to `ethan@apartmentcorp.com` only and were accepted by Gmail. The report designs, layouts, and card conventions were not touched.

I verified the link target independently before it was wired in: `vacancyreport.manus.space` renders "Updated: Nov 4, 2026 11:06 PM" with 115 vacant, whereas the old `vacancyapp-42vudntx.manus.space` still shows July 24, 2026.

## Two things you should know

**One real risk remains open.** The task disabled every legacy sender inside the app, but it could not confirm the status of the **external Railway trigger** — the Railway dashboard needs a login it doesn't have. If that trigger is still armed, you could get a duplicate Collections email at 1 PM. Worth a look at the Railway service to confirm the cron is deleted, or hand over access so it can be verified properly.

**A bug surfaced during the test.** Visual review of the Vacancy test found a column-mapping error in the unit-detail rows — a percentage rendering under "Move Out," for example. That's a data presentation defect in the Vacancy email, not something the migration introduced, and the task is already tracing it. Good thing the tests were forced to Ethan-only.

The full migration record and the two test HTML files live in that task's workspace (`vacancy-report/managed_daily_reports_completion.md`), reachable from the Vacancy Report App task.
